clue.text: He helps others cope with the ups and downs of navigation

definitions.text: He helps others cope with the ups and downs of navigation

parts.words: He helps others cope with the ups and downs of navigation
parts.note: the ups and downs are boats rising and falling in a canal chamber, which this worker operates for passing craft

explanation.surface: Someone supports others through the emotional ups and downs of finding their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ups and downs' sounds like life's troubles, but on a canal boats are literally raised and lowered by the gates this person works.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal attendant works the gates that let boats climb or descend between water levels.

clue.text: Bound to name Spanish dramatist

definitions.meaning: to bound is to run with long easy strides
... de Vega, the prolific Golden Age Spanish playwright

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to identify a Spanish playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: A long striding run is a lope, and Lope de Vega is Spain's great Golden Age playwright.

clue.text: Within reason, men turned up to drink freely

indicators.note: the men are placed within the word for reason

parts.note: a reason is a cause

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word for men is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Within reason, some men arrived to have a good drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses OR to RO, which goes inside CAUSE. OR (other ranks) is a crossword staple for men.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink heavily and merrily, a synonym of drinking freely.

clue.text: Broadcasting networks hope to be expert

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so the letters of the two words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Television networks hope their broadcasting will show expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' fits the networks so well it reads as plain description, but it rearranges NETWORKS HOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To know the ropes is an idiom for being experienced and expert at something.

clue.text: Make very thin English china foreign agents imported

indicators.note: imported means brought into something, so the agents go inside the word for china

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a friend
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, foreign agents from a British view

explanation.surface: English porcelain is smuggled in by overseas spies, making it thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like porcelain but is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate); the surface's foreign agents bringing in porcelain hides the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to waste a body away until it is gaunt and skeletal.

clue.text: One whose trips are image-building

parts.note: trips that build one's image are ego trips, taken by a self-centred person

explanation.surface: Someone travels to improve their public image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' suggests journeys, but the phrase meant is an ego trip, an act of self-promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person preoccupied with their own importance goes on ego trips.

clue.text: It shows the pitch's cracked, unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word for cracked is cut off

parts.note: cleft means split or cracked

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch is shown to be cracked and incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports ground, but it is musical pitch, which a stave's symbol fixes. 'unfinished' drops the T of CLEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: In music notation the symbol at the start of a stave sets which notes the lines stand for.

clue.text: Plain man writing lines on a tyrant

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
Nero was the notoriously cruel Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An ordinary man writes lines about a despot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like ordinary, but it is a grassland plain: a llanero is a herdsman of the South American llanos.
explanation.definitionFit: A llanero is a cowboy of the Venezuelan and Colombian grassland plains, the llanos.

clue.text: Like post needed asap in kindergarten

definitions.meaning: urgent mail goes by the faster, dearer service of British post
the lowest class at school is the earliest, so its pupils are in the opening year

explanation.surface: Mail needed urgently at a nursery school.
explanation.walkthrough: British Royal Mail sells two tiers of stamp; the faster one is named this.
explanation.definitionFit: The faster British postal tier and the earliest school class both carry this ordinal label.

clue.text: One makes a hole for each loudspeaker

annotationWithheld.why: One makes a hole for each loudspeaker (10): 'for each' gives PER and 'loudspeaker' ORATOR, but no clue word supplies the F between them; likely a word dropped in OCR, and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: One makes a hole for each loudspeaker

clue.text: Within three, four, or five, one or two

indicators.note: one is placed within the word that the golf scores describe

parts.note: par for a golf hole is three, four or five strokes
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about numbers inside three, four or five.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers read like arithmetic, but they are the possible par scores of a golf hole; I goes inside PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple of matching things make a set of two.

clue.text: Boycott stupid person's meat product

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as unions blacked goods
a pudding is a dull, slow-witted person

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott calls someone a fool over a meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Boycott suggests the Yorkshire cricketer, but it is the verb, to black. Black pudding is a British blood sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Black pudding is a British sausage made from pig's blood, fat and oatmeal.

clue.text: Broken sculpture

definitions.meaning: ... means broken, as in a ... machine

explanation.surface: A damaged statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for broken, and also a sculpted head and shoulders.

clue.text: Bankrupt at home getting thinner

parts.note: in means at home
a paint thinner is a solvent

explanation.surface: Someone at home growing slimmer has gone broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thinner' reads as slimmer, but it is the liquid used to dilute paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to pay their debts is legally bankrupt.

clue.text: She's specially suited for long-distance travel

definitions.text: She's specially suited for long-distance travel

parts.words: She's specially suited for long-distance travel
parts.note: suited is literal: she wears a pressure suit for journeys beyond Earth

explanation.surface: A woman who is naturally fit for long journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suited' seems to mean well fitted, but she literally wears a special suit for travel off the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A female astronaut wears a pressurised suit for journeys beyond the atmosphere.

clue.text: Moral instructions for rate collections

definitions.meaning: a precept was an order from a council to collect local rates, the old British property tax

explanation.surface: Ethical guidance about collecting local taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were a British local property tax; a precept was the demand ordering their collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules for conduct are maxims; a rating authority's demand for money had the same name.

clue.text: Group of gamblers in coach

definitions.meaning: a set of people gambling together, as a poker circle

explanation.surface: Some gamblers travelling on a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling circle shares its name with the verb meaning to train or teach.

clue.text: Fierce old girl tormented, we hear, a nervous head

indicators.note: we hear means the word for tormented is given as it is spoken

parts.note: harried means harassed or tormented

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word nervous

explanation.surface: A fierce old woman, tormented, has a nervous head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns HARRIED into its sound HARRID; then A and N, the head of 'nervous'.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, belligerent old woman, a shrewish crone.

clue.text: Frequent recreation area

definitions.meaning: public land in a town, as a village green

explanation.surface: A park that is often visited.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary or frequent, and also shared open land in a British town.

clue.text: Cosmetic mother used to cover a blemish

parts.note: ma is mother
a scar is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: A mother uses make-up to hide a skin mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests concealer hiding a scar; the answer is in fact eyelash make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is make-up applied to darken eyelashes.

clue.text: Small swimmers — little perches

parts.note: a tad is a little
a pole or perch is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Tiny swimmers rest on little perches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perches' looks like bird roosts, but a perch is an old unit of length, also called a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Young frogs swim as tailed larvae before growing legs.

clue.text: High court action by author is a bloomer

parts.note: a lob is a high shot on a tennis court
Elia was the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A legal case brought in the High Court by a writer is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High court' suggests law; it is a tennis court. 'bloomer' is a mistake on the surface, but a flowering plant here.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobelia is a flowering garden plant, so it blooms.

clue.text: Men she contrived to catch

indicators.note: contrived means artfully arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman schemes to trap men.
explanation.definitionFit: To enmesh is to entangle in a net, to trap.

clue.text: His home is left on the map

definitions.text: His home is left on the map

parts.words: His home is left on the map
parts.note: left on the map is the west side, since maps put north at the top

explanation.surface: A man's home has been omitted from the map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' suggests omitted, but it means the left-hand, westerly side of a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from the western regions lives on the left of a north-up map.

clue.text: Prints produced by experts

definitions.meaning: a dab hand, or dab, is an expert

explanation.surface: Prints made by specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for fingerprints, and also for skilled hands.

clue.text: Knowing chief at the start and ruler at the end

definitions.meaning: ... means knowing or roguish, as an ... look
as a prefix it means chief, as in archbishop
as a suffix it means ruler, as in monarch

explanation.surface: A knowing leader opens and a ruler closes.
explanation.definitionFit: Roguish and knowing, and also a word part meaning chief at the front or ruler at the back.

clue.text: Name old bird initially as grouse

indicators.note: initially means the bird comes first, before the abbreviation for name

parts.note: the moa is an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: Identify an ancient bird, first of all, as a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the game bird beside 'old bird', but it is the verb to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to complain or grumble.

clue.text: Destroyer made for the docks, for example

definitions.text: Destroyer made for the docks, for example

parts.words: Destroyer made for the docks, for example
parts.note: docks are weeds, not harbours, and a destroyer here is not a warship but a garden chemical

explanation.surface: A warship built to serve at the dockyards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer' and 'docks' paint a naval scene, but dock is a broad-leaved weed.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbicide destroys unwanted plants such as dock.

clue.text: Boat-builder located in Genoa harbour

indicators.note: located in says the answer sits within the run of the two words

explanation.surface: A shipwright based in the harbour of Genoa.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah built the ark in the Book of Genesis.

clue.text: Sort of pencil mate used with chart

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate
a graph is a chart

explanation.surface: A friend draws a chart with a pencil.
explanation.walkthrough: china = mate is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate).
explanation.definitionFit: A chinagraph is a waxy pencil for writing on glass or china.
